title: District anchor x/y loaded unvalidated; new map_district_assign converts them via unchecked i32(math.round(f64*10))
evidence:
core/map.odin loader (type check only, no range check):
		px, okx := doj["x"].(json.Float)
		py, oky := doj["y"].(json.Float)
		if !okx || !oky {
			return map_board_load_fail(&b, "map_board_load: district missing x/y")
		}
...
		append(&b.districts, Map_District{name = strings_clone(name, allocator), kind = kind, pos = {f32(px), f32(py)}})

core/map.odin map_district_assign (new in this chunk — the consumer):
		ax := i32(math.round(f64(b.districts[d].pos[0]) * MAP_ANCHOR_SCALE))
		ay := i32(math.round(f64(b.districts[d].pos[1]) * MAP_ANCHOR_SCALE))
		dx := i64(pos[0]) * MAP_ANCHOR_SCALE - i64(ax)
detail: Anchor x/y accept any float (e.g. 1e30); the new nearest-anchor math converts via unchecked i32(round(f64*10)) — an out-of-range float→int conversion is implementation-defined. Every sibling loader field is fail-fast validated; this one is not.
recommended_fix: Range-validate district x/y at load (0 <= x < map_w_tiles, 0 <= y < map_h_tiles, fail-fast like board dims), so anchors never reach the integer conversion unchecked.
